candidates: Avoid embedding roughjs calls directly inside individual shape rendering functions; keep roughjs interaction centralized or behind an abstraction layer to prevent tight coupling that would be difficult to refactor later.

When implementing multiple shape rendering functions, extract shared logic (e.g., roughjs wrapper creation, bounding-box setup, label insertion boilerplate) into shared utilities rather than duplicating it across each shape file.
Use kebab-case exclusively for all shape names and aliases registered in the shapes module (e.g., `my-new-shape`, not `myNewShape`); do not register camelCase variants alongside kebab-case variants.

Shape names must not contain underscores (`_`); add validation in the shape-registration layer (e.g., `flowDb.ts`) to reject any shape name that contains an underscore, since some legacy shapes carry them.

In the flowchart parser (`flow.jison` and related grammar files), handle both `
` and `
` when detecting line endings—checking for `
` alone breaks Windows users.

Standardize the signature of every shape rendering function to accept a third parameter of a named, reusable type (e.g., `ShapeRenderOptions`) that carries `config`; do not call `getConfig()` inside shape functions, as this will block future parallel-rendering work.
Do not call `getConfig()` (or any other global-config accessor) inside a loop; hoist the call outside the loop and reuse the returned value.

When accessing properties on an object that may be `undefined`, be consistent: either add an early-return guard (`if (!vertex) return`) and remove all `?.` on that object's accesses, or apply `?.` uniformly to every access. Do not mix optional and non-optional access on the same nullable object, as this creates false safety.
Documentation files and directories must use kebab-case naming (e.g., `adding-new-shape.md`, not `adding_new_shape/Readme.md`), consistent with URL conventions used elsewhere in the project.
Use `pnpm` (not `npm` or `yarn`) for all install and run commands shown in project documentation.
Use the `<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>` placeholder token—not hardcoded version numbers—when referencing the Mermaid release version in documentation headings and prose.

Before removing or replacing shape registrations in the shapes module, verify that no existing diagrams rely on the removed names by checking the full alias list and running regression tests to confirm backward compatibility.

Before introducing a new type or interface name, search the codebase for existing declarations of that name to avoid duplicate or conflicting types; use a more specific name (e.g., `ShapeRenderOptions` instead of `RenderOptions`) when a collision exists.
